entries.definition: A bundle of groups, applications, SharePoint sites and roles that users request as one unit, governed by policies defining who may request, approvals, duration and recertification.
A Defender for Cloud Apps rule applied at sign-in through the reverse proxy that allows or blocks entry to a cloud app based on user, device, location or client app.

A scheduled or one-time recertification in which reviewers confirm whether users still need group memberships, app assignments, access package assignments or privileged roles, so stale access gets removed.
A sync safeguard that halts export when a single cycle would remove more objects than a configured threshold, 500 by default, protecting the tenant from mass deletions caused by misconfiguration.
The PIM step where a user with an eligible role requests to use it for a bounded period, up to 24 hours, meeting configured MFA, justification, ticket or approval requirements.
A PIM role grant whose permissions are usable immediately without any activation step, either permanently or until a set end date; it creates standing privilege and should be used sparingly.
A Defender for Cloud Apps rule that inspects activities collected through API connectors and alerts or acts when a pattern appears, such as mass downloads or admin actions from a risky IP address.

Approval by a privileged administrator granting an application the requested permissions for the whole organization; it is required for application permissions and for high-impact delegated permissions.
A request process letting users who cannot approve an app themselves submit a justification that designated reviewers can approve or deny, rather than users being blocked outright.

A directory container that groups users, groups or devices so an administrator can be given a role scoped only to those objects, for example letting a regional helpdesk reset passwords for one office without tenant-wide rights.

An API-based integration between Defender for Cloud Apps and a sanctioned service such as Microsoft 365 or Salesforce, giving visibility into activities, files and accounts for governance and threat detection.

A Defender for Cloud Apps capability that monitors OAuth-enabled apps registered in Microsoft Entra ID, profiling their permissions, data use and behavior and applying policies to detect and disable risky ones.

The global definition of an application in its home tenant, holding the client ID, credentials, redirect URIs, API permissions, app roles and supported account types used to request tokens from the Microsoft identity platform.

A role defined in an application's registration, such as Reader or Approver, assignable to users, groups or other applications and delivered in the token's roles claim so the app can authorize actions.
An app-only permission used by background services or daemons running with no signed-in user; it applies across the tenant's data and always requires admin consent.

A lightweight agent installed on Windows Server inside the corporate network that makes outbound-only connections to the cloud service to publish internal web apps for secure remote access without inbound firewall ports.

The rules attached to an access package defining who can request it, required approvers, requestor questions, assignment expiration and periodic reviews; one package can have several for different audiences.
The record of changes made in the directory, such as user, group, application, role and policy updates, showing who made each change, when and to which object; free tenants retain it seven days.

A labeled tag (c1 to c99) that apps, sensitivity-labeled SharePoint sites or PIM activations can request, triggering a Conditional Access policy that demands stronger controls only for sensitive data or actions.

The central configuration where each sign-in and recovery method, such as Authenticator, passkeys, TAP or SMS, is enabled or disabled and targeted to groups, replacing the legacy per-user MFA and SSPR method settings.

A Conditional Access grant control listing which sign-in method combinations satisfy a policy; built-in options are multifactor, passwordless multifactor and phishing-resistant multifactor, and custom combinations are possible.
A recertification setting that automatically removes denied, and optionally unreviewed, access when the review ends, instead of requiring an administrator to apply decisions manually.
A service that creates, updates and disables accounts in SaaS applications, typically via SCIM, based on assignments and scoping filters, so leavers lose access in connected apps automatically.
Portal actions that create, invite, delete or add many users or group members at once by uploading a CSV template, with results downloadable for verification.
An entitlement management container holding resources and the access packages built from them, whose owners and access package managers receive delegated rights to administer just that set.

Signing in with an X.509 certificate, such as on a smart card, validated against certificate authorities uploaded to the tenant; binding rules decide whether it counts as single-factor or multifactor.

A generated string password an application presents to prove its identity when requesting tokens; it must expire and be rotated, and certificates or federated credentials are preferred as safer alternatives.
Defender for Cloud Apps' database of tens of thousands of services, each scored for risk across security, compliance and legal factors, used to evaluate and sanction or unsanction discovered apps.
Defender for Cloud Apps analysis of firewall or proxy traffic logs, or of Defender for Endpoint signals, to reveal which cloud services employees actually use, exposing shadow IT and its risk.

A Microsoft Entra provisioning option using lightweight agents with configuration held in the cloud; it supports disconnected forests and high availability through multiple agents, but has fewer features than Connect Sync.
Tenant sign-in page customization such as logo, background image, colors and sign-in text, giving users a familiar look that helps them recognize the genuine organizational sign-in experience.
Defender for Cloud Apps reverse-proxy capability that, when a Conditional Access session control routes a user to it, monitors and controls browser sessions in real time.

An administrator action in ID Protection that marks a user or sign-in as truly malicious, raising user risk to high and feeding the decision back into Microsoft's machine learning; the opposite is confirming safe.
A Microsoft Entra monitoring service using installed agents to report the health, performance, alerts and sync errors of Connect sync servers, AD FS and domain controllers.

An external directory or domain registered in entitlement management so its users can request access packages; accounts are created as guests on approval and can be removed when their last assignment ends.
A named set of private network connectors that serve particular published apps, providing high availability and letting traffic be routed through connectors in the right network location or site.

A mechanism where supporting services receive critical events, such as account disable, password change or network location change, and reject tokens almost immediately instead of waiting for them to expire.

Default and per-organization inbound and outbound controls for B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect, specifying which users, groups and applications may collaborate and which external claims are trusted.

An automated provisioning service, configured in the source tenant and allowed by the target tenant, that creates, updates and removes B2B accounts for users across Microsoft Entra tenants in the same organization, by default as external members.

Up to 1,000 organization-specific words, such as brand or product names, that Password Protection rejects together with Microsoft's global list and common variations, in the cloud and on domain controllers with the agent.

An organization-owned DNS name added to the tenant and proven by publishing a TXT or MX record, so user sign-in names and email addresses can use the company's own name instead of the onmicrosoft.com suffix.

An administrator-defined Microsoft Entra role built from a chosen set of granular permissions, used when no built-in role matches the job closely enough to honor least privilege; it can be assigned tenant-wide or at a narrower scope.

A business-defined key-value property, grouped into attribute sets, stored on users and enterprise applications; reading or assigning it needs dedicated attribute roles, and it can drive Azure attribute-based access control or filter apps in Conditional Access.

Tenant settings that limit what ordinary members can do by default, such as registering applications, creating tenants or security groups, and reading other users, tightened to shrink the attack surface.
A permission an app uses to act on behalf of a signed-in user; its effective access is the overlap between what the app was granted and what the user is personally allowed to do.

Giving a personal or bring-your-own device an identity in Microsoft Entra ID while the user still signs in locally with their own account, enabling device-based Conditional Access and Intune management of work data.

The Microsoft Entra configuration that streams log categories such as audit, sign-in and provisioning logs to a Log Analytics workspace, storage account, event hub or partner solution for retention and analysis.

A PIM view summarizing privileged role assignments, highlighting permanent Global Administrators and other standing privileged access, with guidance to reduce exposure or convert assignments to eligible.

An attribute-based expression, such as user.department -eq "Sales", that automatically adds and removes users or devices from a group as their properties change, keeping access aligned with HR data without manual edits.
A PIM role grant that does not give permissions until the user activates it for a limited time, satisfying requirements such as MFA, justification or approval, minimizing standing privilege.
A fallback sign-in method for external collaborators who have no Microsoft Entra, Microsoft or federated account: a temporary code is emailed to them each time they need to authenticate.

A highly privileged, cloud-only break-glass account with strong phishing-resistant credentials, excluded from policies that could lock everyone out, closely monitored and used only when normal administration fails.
The portal view of an app's service principal in your tenant, where administrators configure single sign-on, user and group assignment, provisioning, consent and Conditional Access targeting.
Tenant-wide guest controls covering how much guests can see in the directory, who may send invitations, whether one-time passcodes are enabled, and allow or deny lists of collaborating domains.
A hybrid model in which the cloud hands sign-in requests to a separate trusted identity provider, such as AD FS, that verifies credentials and issues tokens; it adds infrastructure to maintain.

A trust configured on an app registration or user-assigned managed identity that accepts tokens from an external issuer, such as GitHub Actions or Kubernetes, in exchange for access tokens, eliminating stored secrets.

A Conditional Access condition that includes or excludes devices using a rule on device attributes, such as model, trust type or extension attributes, for example to target privileged access workstations.

A pre-integrated SaaS app template from the Microsoft Entra catalog that comes with ready-made single sign-on and often provisioning settings, simplifying integration compared with a custom non-gallery app.
Software installed on Windows, macOS, iOS or Android devices that acquires and tunnels traffic matching enabled forwarding profiles to Microsoft's Security Service Edge for policy enforcement.

The part of a Conditional Access policy that blocks access or requires conditions to be met, such as MFA, an authentication strength, a compliant or hybrid joined device, approved apps or a password change.

Assigning product licenses to a group so every member automatically receives them and loses them on removal, with options to disable individual service plans and reports for assignment errors like insufficient license counts.

An external person invited into the tenant through B2B collaboration who authenticates with their own home identity; the account typically has the userType Guest and restricted default directory permissions.

A Windows device joined to on-premises Active Directory Domain Services and also registered in Microsoft Entra ID, typically via synchronization, so existing domain machines can satisfy device-based Conditional Access requirements.
A percentage measuring how closely the tenant follows Microsoft's identity security best practices, with improvement actions such as protecting admins with MFA that raise it as they are completed.

Options in cross-tenant access that let Conditional Access accept another tenant's multifactor authentication, compliant device or hybrid joined device claims, so external users are not forced to repeat MFA in your tenant.
The Global Secure Access secure web gateway that inspects users' traffic to public websites and SaaS apps, applying web content filtering and Conditional Access to internet destinations.

The step where an invited external person accepts access, signs in with a supported identity provider and consents to the permissions the inviting organization requests, after which their account becomes usable.
The principle of granting privileges only at the moment they are needed and only for a short duration, eliminating standing admin rights that attackers could exploit.
The read-only query language used in Log Analytics, Sentinel and workbooks to filter, summarize and join identity log tables such as SigninLogs and AuditLogs.
An offline user risk detection raised when a user's valid username and password pair is found in dark web or paste site dumps; it requires password hash sync for hybrid accounts.

Older protocols such as POP, IMAP, SMTP AUTH and basic authentication that cannot perform multifactor prompts; attackers use them for password spray, so Conditional Access policies commonly block them via the client apps condition.
An automated joiner, mover or leaver process triggered by attributes such as employeeHireDate, running tasks like generating a TAP, sending a welcome email or removing group memberships.
An Azure Monitor data store that receives routed identity logs and is queried with KQL, providing longer retention, alerting and the data source for Entra workbooks and Microsoft Sentinel.

A collaboration group that provisions a shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site and optional Teams workspace for its members; it supports expiration and naming policies but cannot contain devices or nested groups.

An organization-owned Windows device whose local sign-in uses the user's cloud work account, with no on-premises Active Directory join required, giving single sign-on to cloud resources and full device-based policy control.
Personalized, prioritized improvement suggestions generated from tenant configuration and activity, such as removing unused apps or renewing expiring credentials, with status tracking for each item.
An entitlement management request flow with up to three sequential approval steps, each with its own approvers, decision deadline and optional alternate approvers for escalation.
An app registration whose supported account types include any Microsoft Entra directory, so users from other organizations can sign in and a service principal is created in each consenting tenant.

A defined set of Microsoft Entra tenants belonging to one company that are linked so people collaborate more seamlessly in Teams and other Microsoft 365 apps, usually with synchronized member accounts between them.
The end-user web portal where people browse and request access packages, track request status, approve requests assigned to them and complete recertification tasks.
The end-user web portal where people launch applications assigned to them, request access, manage group memberships and update their account settings.
An admin-defined set of IP ranges or countries used as a Conditional Access condition; ranges marked trusted also lower ID Protection's risk calculation for sign-ins from them.
An authentication performed by a client on a user's behalf without any user input, such as silent token refresh, logged separately because volumes are high and patterns can reveal token misuse.
An Authenticator push protection where the user must type the two-digit value shown on the sign-in screen into the app, defeating MFA fatigue attacks where users approve prompts they did not start.
A Defender for Cloud Apps rule that alerts on or revokes third-party apps authorized through OAuth based on requested permissions, community use or user count, countering illicit consent grants.

Extra token contents, such as email, UPN variants, IP address or directory extension attributes, configured on an app registration so the application receives the information it needs for authorization decisions.

A hybrid sign-in method in which lightweight on-premises agents validate passwords directly against Active Directory over outbound-only connections, so no password hash is stored in the cloud and on-premises account policies apply instantly.

A FIDO2 credential built on public-key cryptography, stored on a security key, in Microsoft Authenticator or another credential manager, that is bound to the sign-in origin, making it phishing-resistant and passwordless.
A hybrid sign-in method in which a salted hash of each on-premises password hash is synced to Microsoft Entra ID, letting the cloud verify passwords itself and enabling leaked-credential detection.

A synchronization option that writes password changes and resets made in the cloud, such as through self-service reset, back to on-premises Active Directory so both directories keep the same password.
Labeling selected delegated permissions as low impact so that, under the appropriate consent settings, users may approve apps requesting only those permissions.

A Conditional Access session control deciding whether users stay signed in after closing and reopening their browser, typically set to never persist on unmanaged devices; it requires targeting all resources.
Privileged Identity Management for group membership or ownership, giving just-in-time, time-bound access to whatever a group grants, such as Azure roles, Entra roles or app access.

The Global Secure Access zero-trust service replacing traditional VPNs, giving identity-centric, per-app access to internal resources through private network connectors, with Conditional Access applied to each application.

Selected Microsoft Entra admin permissions, such as changing Conditional Access policies, linked to an authentication context so administrators must meet extra policy requirements at the moment they perform them.
The record of actions by the provisioning service, such as accounts created, updated or skipped in SaaS apps, cross-tenant sync or HR-driven inbound provisioning, used to troubleshoot failures.

The registered address to which the identity platform returns authorization codes or tokens after sign-in; requests with unregistered addresses are refused, preventing tokens from being sent to attackers.
A setting that nudges users during sign-in to set up Microsoft Authenticator or another stronger method, with a configurable number of allowed snoozes, to move people off weaker options such as SMS.
A Conditional Access policy state that evaluates and logs what the policy would have done at each sign-in without enforcing it, so administrators can assess impact before turning it on.

A protected scoping container whose member objects can be changed only by administrators assigned at that container's scope; tenant-level admins, including Global Administrators, cannot modify them, which shields sensitive accounts from broad admin roles.
Decision helpers shown to reviewers that suggest approve or deny based on signals like no sign-in in the last 30 days or low affiliation with the user's peers.
Designated people who receive recertification tasks when the intended reviewers, such as group owners or managers, do not exist for a given user or resource.

An individual suspicious event flagged by ID Protection, such as password spray, unfamiliar sign-in properties or anomalous token, computed in real time or offline and contributing to user or sign-in risk levels.

A service principal flagged by ID Protection for suspicious activity, such as leaked credentials or anomalous sign-ins; investigation and risk-based policy for it require the Workload Identities Premium license.
Per-role PIM configuration controlling maximum activation duration, MFA or authentication context on activation, justification, ticket information, approvers, assignment expiration and notifications.

A group created with the isAssignableToRole flag so Microsoft Entra roles can be granted to it; the flag cannot be changed afterwards and only privileged administrators or owners can alter its membership, preventing privilege escalation.

A hybrid feature that signs users on domain-joined corporate desktops into cloud apps automatically using a Kerberos ticket issued for the AZUREADSSO computer account, working alongside password hash sync or pass-through authentication.
A group type used to grant access to resources, apps, licenses and policies; it has no shared mailbox or collaboration workspace and can contain users, devices, service principals and other groups.
A recertification style in which each user attests whether they still need their own access, useful for guests and broad groups where no owner knows each member.

A capability that lets users reset forgotten passwords or unlock their accounts after proving identity with registered methods, reducing helpdesk calls; with writeback it also updates on-premises Active Directory.
An entitlement management setting marking access packages or groups as incompatible, so a user who already holds one cannot request the other, reducing toxic access combinations.

The local instance of an application in a specific tenant that holds its sign-in, role and permission grants there; it is created when an app is registered or consented to, and a managed identity has one too.

The part of a Conditional Access policy that limits the experience after sign-in, including sign-in frequency, persistent browser behavior, app-enforced restrictions, Defender for Cloud Apps routing and token binding.
A Defender for Cloud Apps rule applied inside a proxied browser session that monitors or restricts actions in real time, such as blocking downloads of sensitive files on unmanaged devices.

A Conditional Access session control setting how long before a user must authenticate again, in hours or days, or every time, for example forcing fresh credentials for sensitive apps or unmanaged devices.
The record of authentication events for users, service principals and managed identities, showing app, location, device, result, MFA details and which Conditional Access policies applied.

ID Protection's estimate that a particular authentication attempt was not made by the legitimate account owner, based on signals like anonymous IP or atypical travel, usually remediated in real time by requiring MFA.

Cloud protection that temporarily locks out sign-in attempts after repeated failures, 10 by default, distinguishing familiar from unfamiliar locations so attackers are blocked while the genuine user can keep signing in.
Synchronization logic that links an incoming on-premises user to an existing cloud-only user by matching the primary SMTP address or userPrincipalName when no immutable anchor link exists yet.
An immutable attribute, by default ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid, that permanently links an on-premises directory object to its cloud counterpart so the pairing survives renames and other attribute changes.

A migration feature that moves selected groups of users from federated sign-in to cloud authentication with password hash sync or pass-through authentication, testing the change before converting the whole domain.
An automatically managed credential enabled directly on one Azure resource, sharing that resource's lifecycle so it is deleted with it; the resource uses it to get tokens without storing secrets.
A setting that makes sign-in prompt the user for the most secure second factor they have registered, rather than the method they chose as default, steering them away from weaker phone-based options.

A time-limited, admin-issued passcode, usable once or multiple times, that counts as strong authentication so users can onboard passwordless methods or recover access without needing an existing second factor.
A PDF agreement users must accept before accessing resources, enforced as a Conditional Access grant control, with options for per-device acceptance, expiration, re-acceptance and acceptance reports.
A Conditional Access session control that binds sign-in session tokens cryptographically to the device they were issued to, so stolen tokens replayed from another device are rejected.

A Global Secure Access setting determining which network traffic the client or remote network tunnels to Microsoft's edge: the Microsoft traffic profile, the Private Access profile or the Internet Access profile.
A tag in Defender for Cloud Apps marking a discovered cloud service as prohibited, which can generate block scripts for network appliances or block it on devices through Defender for Endpoint.
A set of Microsoft Entra reports showing patterns such as authentication method registration and use, application sign-in activity and service principal sign-ins, to guide adoption and cleanup.
An enterprise application property that, when set to Yes, issues tokens only to users, groups or apps explicitly assigned to it, instead of letting anyone in the tenant sign in.

An individual granting an application delegated access to their own data; tenant settings can block it or limit it to verified publishers requesting low-impact permissions, reducing illicit consent grant risk.

ID Protection's estimate that an account itself is compromised, raised by detections such as leaked credentials; risk policies typically remediate it by requiring a secure password change or blocking access.

A standalone Azure resource holding an automatically managed credential that can be attached to many Azure resources and survives their deletion, useful when several resources need the same permissions.
Internet Access policies that allow or block destinations by web category or fully qualified domain name, grouped into security profiles and applied to users through Conditional Access.
A Conditional Access troubleshooting simulator where an admin supplies a user, application and conditions such as location, platform or risk to see which policies would apply and which would not.
A passwordless Windows sign-in that replaces the password with a PIN or biometric unlocking a hardware-protected key pair bound to that device, providing phishing-resistant authentication.
An interactive Azure Monitor report built on routed log data, with ready-made templates such as sign-in analysis and Conditional Access insights, for visualizing identity activity and trends.

An identity used by software rather than a person, such as an application, service principal or managed identity, to authenticate and access resources; it cannot perform MFA, so it needs credential hygiene and monitoring.
